claims: Effective April 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of State has reduced the fee for renouncing U.S. citizenship to $450.
The previous fee for renouncing U.S. citizenship was $2,350.
The reduction in the fee for renouncing U.S. citizenship is 80%.
The 80% reduction applies to the administrative processing of a Certificate of Loss of Nationality.
The in-person process for renouncing U.S. citizenship requires appearing at a U.S. embassy or consulate outside the U.S.
The U.S. Department of State published a final rule in March 2026 to bring the fee back to 2010 levels.
The fee for Certificate of Loss of Nationality services is non-refundable, even if the request is denied.
The previous high fee for renouncing U.S. citizenship was introduced in 2015 to cover administrative costs.
Renunciation of U.S. citizenship requires appearing in person before a U.S. consular or diplomatic officer in a foreign country.
Renunciation of U.S. citizenship does not exempt a person from past taxes.
A person must be tax-compliant for the 5 years preceding renunciation of U.S. citizenship.
A person with net worth over $2 million or average tax liability might be considered a covered expatriate subject to an exit tax upon renouncing U.S. citizenship.
Renunciation of U.S. citizenship is generally irrevocable.
